name: door
description: Which one-way door this unit passes through, or that it passes through none.

aiGuidance.purpose: Marks the irreversibility of a unit. A door is a commitment that is expensive or impossible to walk back — a published identifier, a corpus-wide data migration, a contract other repositories consume. Numbering them lets the programme order the reversible work before the doors and stage the doors themselves; non-normative marks a unit that changes nothing anyone depends on and can be redone freely.
aiGuidance.extraction: Ask what someone outside this repository would have to change if the unit were reverted. Nothing outside changes means non-normative. Where the source explicitly names a door, use that number; where it describes an irreversible commitment without numbering it, assign the door of the commitment it is part of rather than inventing a new one.
aiGuidance.negativeGuidance: Effort is not irreversibility — a large but freely redoable rewrite is non-normative. Do not mark a unit as a door merely because it is important.
